voiceControl: warm confident product-demo narrator explaining a spatial tool to a colleague; clear friendly English; measured pace; natural pauses; light emphasis on key evidence; not dramatic; do not read like a slide deck

segments.text: A Gaussian-splat capture can show a place beautifully and still tell an agent almost nothing about what the place means. This is SceneIndex.
The page combines Gaussian appearance with persistent rooms, objects, relationships, routes, operational state, and capture evidence. The person and the agent work on the same live scene.
I will ask for an accessible route from Entrance A to Platform 2 and ask whether the evidence is trustworthy.

The agent reads the current page, finds the accessible gate, moves the shared camera, and draws a route through Lift 1. The result is visible and inspectable. It is not a route hidden in a backend response.
Now I change the situation. Lift 1 is unavailable. The agent stages that state on the page. The lift turns red, and the change remains reversible.

The original path is no longer valid. The new route uses Lift 2, but the West corridor has only 56 percent accessible-wayfinding readiness. Connectivity is known. The sign text is not visually verified.
The agent opens the capture evidence instead of guessing. The page highlights the weak region and explains the unreadable sign and single-view coverage gap.
It recommends a front-facing sign capture and a reverse corridor pass from the Lift 2 side. Capture quality becomes a task-specific decision, not one opaque percentage.
I can inspect, accept, or undo every change. Undo restores the baseline scene without reloading the page.
The app exposes ten narrow tools through the current imperative WebMCP API. Human controls and agent calls share the same runtime, validation, viewer effects, and visible timeline.
The app, source, license, tests, provenance, and build receipts are public. Search a place. Understand it. Test what happens when it changes.
